source_graph.source_title: Accelerated High-Accuracy Sampling from a Warm Start via the Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler

nodes.statement: V is C2 on R^d, 0<alpha<=beta, alpha I <= Hess V(x) <= beta I for every x; mu is normalized exp(-V) dx.
nodes.eta_condition: eta in (0,1/beta], equivalently eta>0 and beta eta<=1 for this selected lemma
no_extra_regularities: no spectral basis/rank or nonzero-dimensional assumption
no warm-start condition is used by B15/B16

nodes.statement: Real scalar-valued L2 of a probability measure consists of measurable functions modulo a.e. equality; bounded operators, adjoints and Loewner order use that Hilbert structure.
nodes.spectral_background: D.1 states bounded Borel functional calculus for self-adjoint operators and existence/uniqueness of the non-negative square root of a non-negative operator. The scalar lower bound on the root is a spectral consequence; D.1 does not separately state arbitrary-pair operator monotonicity.

nodes.statement: X~mu and independent Z~N(0,I), Y+=X+sqrt(eta) Z. pi_eta^Y has curvature at least alpha/(1+alpha eta); conditional laws have the stated potentials.
H=L2(pi_eta), P=conditional expectation given Y, HP=range P identified with L2(pi_eta^Y), Hperp=ker P; the first block index is the target and second is the source.
nodes.centered_domain: HP0=HP intersect L2_0(pi_eta), identified with L2_0(pi_eta^Y); Hperp consists of conditional-mean-zero observables, hence is globally centered.

nodes.statement: Uf(x,y)=f(x,2x-y); preservation and involution imply self-adjoint unitary U. A=UPP is a self-adjoint contraction HP->HP; T=UperpP maps HP->Hperp and T* T=I-A^2.

The exchangeable Y+/Y- pair represents Af as E[f(Y-)|Y+]; ||Tf||^2 is expected conditional variance. Gamma=(I-A^2)^(1/2) is the unique non-negative operator root on HP, T*T=Gamma^2 and ||Tf||=||Gamma f|| for every f in HP.

For smooth compactly supported f, differentiate the normalized conditional density. Its score covariance is the derivative of Af. Conditional strong convexity, Hessian bounds and beta eta<=1 bound directional score variance; conditional Cauchy-Schwarz and integration yield C.2.
nodes.regularity: The proof explicitly extends the smooth calculation to all L2 f by density and closedness of the gradient. Differentiation under the normalized integral, integrable score/covariance and conditional Poincare are required by this route and furnished by the stated C2/Hessian/Gaussian-tail setting.

nodes.statement: For every L2 f, eta ||grad Af||^2 <= (1-alpha eta)^2/[4(1+alpha eta)] ||Tf||^2. In particular Af in H1 and B.13 follows.
not_public_extra_hypotheses: C.2 is an intermediate estimate proved from the source assumptions, not an extra source theorem premise.

nodes.statement: For f in HP0, A fixes constants and is self-adjoint, so Af is centered. Marginal Poincare gives ||Af||^2 <= (1/alpha+eta)||grad Af||^2.
Combining C.2/C.3 and ||Tf||^2=||f||^2-||Af||^2 gives ||Af|| <= rho_mac ||f|| on HP0, rho=(1-alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta). This endpoint includes alpha eta=1 without dividing by rho.

Exchangeability and Gaussian Poincare show <g,(I-A)g><=2 eta||grad g||^2; applying g=Af and B.13 yields (I-A)^2(I+2A)>=0 and Spec(A) subset [-1/2,1]. This proves the separate A>=-I/2 statement and is not necessary for the norm-to-root B15 edge.
On HP0, Gamma=(I-A^2)^(1/2) >= gamma_gap I in Loewner order, gamma_gap=sqrt(1-rho^2)=2 sqrt(alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta)>0.
nodes.exact_sense: For every f in HP0, <f,(Gamma-gamma_gap I)f> >= 0. Gamma is a bounded linear operator on a real scalar-valued-L2 Hilbert space; gamma_gap is a scalar. This source conclusion is not merely a numerical norm-coercivity inequality.
nodes.square-root_step: Self-adjoint centered A and C.4 give I-A^2 >= (1-rho^2)I. Spectral positivity/monotonicity for the unique positive root then gives B.15.
nodes.reducing_space: A fixes constants and preserves centered space. Functional calculus preserves that reducing space; the restriction of the full positive root is the centered positive root.

nodes.statement: Gamma is boundedly invertible on HP0. VperpP=T Gamma^(-1):HP0->Hperp, T=VperpP Gamma on HP0 and VperpP* VperpP=I_HP0.
nodes.inverse_contract: Gamma^(-1) is a genuine bounded two-sided inverse on HP0, not just a scalar reciprocal, arbitrary supplied inverse, one-sided inverse, or inverse on the full macroscopic space.
nodes.analytic_step: The positive centered lower bound yields injectivity and closed range; self-adjointness gives dense range by orthogonal-complement/kernel duality, hence surjectivity and bounded inverse, with norm at most 1/gamma.
nodes.polar_step: For f,g in HP0, <T Gamma^-1 f,T Gamma^-1 g>=<Gamma Gamma^-1 f,Gamma Gamma^-1 g>=<f,g>; thus the normalized leakage is an isometry.

endpoint_legality.alpha_eta_one: Allowed by 0<alpha<=beta and beta eta<=1; it forces alpha=beta=eta^-1, rho=0, gamma=1. C.4 gives centered A=0, hence centered Gamma=I; its inverse and normalized leakage remain legal. No division by rho or 1-alpha eta is needed.
endpoint_legality.rank_zero_or_trivial_space: No nontrivial-dimension or nonzero-rank premise appears in B15/B16. A trivial centered Hilbert space has the unique identity/inverse/isometry statements vacuously. Zero contraction A on a nontrivial centered space yields Gamma=I and is also legal; it does not mean leakage T is zero. A zero leakage T on a nontrivial centered space is incompatible with gamma>0.
endpoint_legality.full_space_failure: On full HP, A1=1, hence Gamma1=0. The nonzero constant vector prevents bounded invertibility there. A full-space inverse is not licensed by the source.
